title: Hot-path exemplar micro-sampling with rollback/backpressure hook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Tracer instrumentation on high-QPS inference hot paths allocates per-request objects when making sampling decisions and attaching exemplars. This causes measurable tail-latency regressions under bursty traffic despite low average CPU usage. Goal: introduce a minimal-effort micro-sampling path that avoids allocations and heavy locks on the hot path, emits lightweight exemplar references, and supports a rollback hook when a later event elevates the request's importance (e.g., elevated error state or policy override).

What we're building: a hot-path exemplar micro-sampler that: (1) makes O(1) sampling decisions using a thread-local LRU token bucket and a fixed-size exemplar slot to avoid heap allocations; (2) records only a tiny exemplar token (opaque 64-bit ID + tiny metadata) in the request context; (3) provides a rollback API that a downstream evaluator (error detector, tail-sampler) can call to turn the exemplar token into a full trace emission; (4) integrates a backpressure hook so the rollback path can reject conversions when the trace emit budget is exhausted, and record a lightweight metric instead.

Design constraints: minimal changes to existing tracer client SDKs, backward-compatible with server-side tail-samplers, and must reduce per-request allocations and mutex contention at 99th percentile. We prefer lock-free or low-contention data structures and avoid copying span payloads until rollback happens.

Scope: SDK changes (go/python/node), ingress-side micro-sampling policy, rollout instrumentation, migration guide for customers who use custom tracers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hot-path memory allocations attributable to tracer sampling path reduced by >= 80% at 99p on benchmark harness (same QPS/size).
2) End-to-end end-user latency (p99) improvement of >= 3-6ms on the conflated workload where tracing previously regressed p99.
3) When rollback is triggered, the full trace is emitted with correct span hierarchy and tags.
4) Rollback rejection metric increments when emit budget is exceeded and does not crash callers.
5) Backward compatibility: services that don't call rollback continue to behave and show same sampling distribution as before (approx).
progress_updates: 2025-02-19: Spike completed — implemented thread-local 64-bit exemplar token and benchmark harness. Observed ~86% allocation reduction in synthetic loop (go tracer).

2025-02-24: Design review with tracing team — agreed to expose Tracer.RollbackExemplar(ctx, token) API that returns (ok, reason). Decided to store minimal metadata (route_id, sampling_reason) in fixed-size ring buffer per-worker.

2025-02-27: Prototype integrated into ingress proxy (go) as a fallback; initial end-to-end tests show rollback success path adds ~1.2ms median cost and ~2.9ms p99 when converting token to full trace (acceptable).
2025-03-03: Found a race when multiple concurrent rollbacks attempt to claim the same exemplar slot; fixed via compare-and-swap and added slow-path lock only for conversion. Added unit tests.
2025-03-04: Preparing PRs for go/python SDKs and ingress; draft dashboards for rollout. Need storage budget limiter and opt-in flag for customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated in SDKs: default off for customers. 2) Stage 0: internal traffic only on canary ingress for 48h with full synthetic load. Monitor allocs, p99 latency, and rollback_rejected. 3) Stage 1: opt-in tenant subset (5% of production) for 72h. 4) Stage 2: progressive ramp to 50% with automated abort if p99 increases >2ms or rollback_rejected rate > 1% of rollbacks. 5) Stage 3: GA with docs and migration guide. Always provide a kill-switch at ingress node level.
risk_mitigation:
- Conversion storm: add per-worker rate limiter and global emit budget.
- Incorrect span context: comprehensive cross-language integration tests; validate trace IDs and parent span relationships in rollback path.
- Memory leak in buffer: fixed-size ring buffer and periodic background sweep; fail-closed on allocation errors.
- Observability blind spot if rollback rejected: increment a counter with sampling of sample payload hashes for offline analysis.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for token lifecycle (issue, hold, convert, expire) across go/python/node.
- Integration tests with ingress proxy and tail-sampler running in k8s test cluster.
- Load test with replayed production trace of QPS spikes to validate p99 and allocs.
- Chaos: simulate rollback service outage and validate fallback metrics and behavior.
notes: Implementation prefers fixed-size C arrays in go tracer to avoid GC churn; python tracer will use pre-allocated bytearray pools. Node tracer to use native buffers. We'll add a compatibility shim for older SDKs to return a no-op token when feature flag off.
